Import Products from CSV

Upload a CSV file to bulk-create products. Required column: name. Optional: sku (PCS barcode), sku_emb, sku_cx, brand, category, cost, price, price_emb, price_carton, emb_per_carton, pcs_per_emb, tax_percent, weight_kg, volume, low_stock, image_url, parent_sku, parent_name, sabor. sku = PCS barcode (main code). sku_emb / sku_cx = optional Embalagem / Caixa barcodes for scanning. To import flavours, put the parent article on its own row, then sabor rows with the same name (or parent_sku / parent_name) and a sabor column (ICE, MAXX MIX, …). Sabores are created under the parent — not as separate articles. Packaging defaults to 1 EMB per Carton and 1 PCS per EMB if left blank. Blank EMB/Carton selling prices are auto-filled from Unit price × packaging. Brand, category, and volume names are matched or created automatically if they do not exist. Use Export All Products to download the current catalog in this same CSV format (parents + sabores linked). Stock quantities are not included and existing products are not changed.

Opening Stock

Enter the starting stock for a shop when opening. For each product fill CX (cartons), EMB (embalagens), and/or PCS (units), plus the CTN / KG Price (carton cost for pack items, or cost per KG for weight items). Total is calculated automatically. For weight (KG) products: enter quantity in the CX / KG column (kilograms) and/or PCS / G (extra grams); EMB is not used. Until the first purchase is recorded, this CTN Price becomes the Last Cost / Rate used by Inventory List, Stock Valuation, Montra, and product cost views. Quantities are added to current stock (so multiple opening files / entries for the same article combine).

Select a shop to begin entering opening stock.

Import Opening Stock from CSV

Bulk-load opening stock for one shop. Required: sku (or name), plus at least one of cx, emb, pcs. Optional: ctn_price (cost price of one carton) — converted to a per-piece cost using the product's packaging so the shop's average cost starts correct. Total PCS = (CX × PCS per Carton) + (EMB × PCS per Embalagem) + PCS.
Important: each import adds the file quantities on top of current stock (does not replace). So Retail file + Warehouse file for the same article both keep their stock combined.

Import Stock Count from CSV

Bulk-upload physically counted quantities for one shop. Required columns: sku (or name) and counted_qty. For weight (KG) products, counted_qty must be in kilograms (e.g. 5.2 for 5.2 KG) and optional unit_cost is cost per KG. Pack/piece products use piece quantities as before. Products are matched by SKU first, then by name. Only rows where the counted quantity differs from the current system quantity create a variance. Add an optional unit_cost column when loading opening stock for a brand-new shop/product — any quantity gained by the count is then costed in at that price. Leave it blank for a routine recount where you only want to correct quantities, not cost.

Counter Day Book

Daily cash account per counter: opening float → cash sales → mid-day cash pickups → close day. Cash Kept at close is tomorrow’s opening. If the manager takes the till overnight, set Cash Kept to 0 (not the old float).

Select a counter and date to open or review the day book.

Open Day Book

Suggested opening comes from yesterday’s Cash Kept. Change it if the manager took the float (enter 0).

Cash Pickups (Deposit)

Cash taken from this counter during the day for bank deposit / manager. Reduces till balance.

Cash Sales Today

Only cash payments increase the till. POS Machine / Deposit are shown for reference.

Close Day Book

Count notes & coins (1000 → 1 MT). Cash Kept for Next Day becomes tomorrow’s opening — use 0 if the manager takes all cash overnight. Amount Received = Declared − Kept.

Profit & Loss Account

Uses each sale's weighted average cost (per shop, snapshotted at sale time — falls back to catalog cost for legacy records). Profit per unit = Selling price − Cost price, then × quantity sold. Use Product Valuation → Recalculate Historical Costs to backfill accurate costs on older transactions. Expenses in the same period are deducted for Net Profit.
